アンソロピックの最先端AIが直面する「安全」と「コスト」のジレンマ 電撃停止が揺るがす上場への成長モデルと、エージェント台頭による企業負担の増大《小久保 重信》@skokubo
米AI新興のアンソロピックによる「Claude Fable（クロード・フェイブル）5」の一般公開は、最先端AIの社会実装がはらむ構造的なジレンマを浮き彫りにした。
同モデルは高い処理能力を示す一方、安全対策の不備を突いた米政府の輸出規制により、公開からわずか3日で電撃的な提供停止に追い込まれる事態となった。
事態はその後、一部モデルの制限解除へと動いたものの、最先端AIのビジネスモデルは依然として深いジレンマの中にある。
また、競合を上回る高額な利用料金は、早期の提供再開を目指す同社にとっても、導入を見据える企業にとってもコスト面の新たな障壁となる。
開発スピードと安全性、経済性のバランスを巡り、最先端AIのビジネスモデルは新たな課題に直面している。
アンソロピックは6月9日、高度なサイバー防御や創薬支援の能力を持つモデル、フェイブル5の一般提供を開始した。
同モデルは、同社が一般公開するには危険すぎると判断していた「Mythos（ミュトス）」を基盤としている。

Évian's Two Dependencies.

SO WHAT FOR LEADERS

👉 The G7 forged a minerals bloc to escape China at the same summit where allies discovered the U.S. could switch off their frontier AI access overnight. Plan for both dependencies at once.

Relief for the minerals risk is now in motion. The model-access risk is not, and it is the one that interrupts operations without warning. Build real portability across providers, open-weight fallbacks, and jurisdictions into anything mission-critical. The firms that dismissed multi-model redundancy as over-engineering just watched it become basic risk management.

For investors, the episode is a tailwind for European and sovereign AI builders, open-weight ecosystems, and compute outside U.S. jurisdiction. On minerals, the IEA platform points capital toward non-Chinese extraction, processing, and recycling. The Macron platform announcement is the policy signal to track.

THE BRIEFING

The G7 in Évian agreed a critical-minerals framework targeting less than 60 percent reliance on any single non-G7 supplier by 2030, with roughly €64 billion already committed across the value chain. The summit was overshadowed by U.S. export controls that had forced Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline worldwide days earlier, cutting off allied users. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind CEOs joined leaders for a working lunch. Amodei urged the group to resist the temptation to splinter. Macron called the order a wake-up call and announced a Western AI cooperation platform within a month.

👉 For more and to subscribe, see link in the comments.

🤖 Can AI Drain DeFi?

The "Claude Mythos" has sparked fears of AI-driven attacks on $DeFi protocols. While the threat is real, security teams are using the same AI tools to harden protocols. It’s a high-tech arms race where defense is fighting back. 🛡️💻

#DeFi #AI

$claude, $anthropic The CA–Anthropic deal reads like a SaaS discount story. It isn't. It's Anthropic's first visible step from model layer → orchestration layer in 2B2G — and that's where durable rent actually lives.

The model layer is the shortest-duration moat in AI: frontier leads get matched in quarters. Real durability comes from converting a fleeting model lead into switching costs before the lead erodes.

Watch the structure: a shared-services procurement portal (SITeS), 50% discount, and a state-built orchestration shell (Poppy). Surface-read: buyer guarding against vendor lock-in. But weak public buyers can't actually build or maintain orchestration alone — which turns "buyer-built" into a Forward-Deployed-Engineer entry point, not a defense. This is the Palantir playbook's opening move.

The prize isn't the smartest model. It's welding Claude into low-digitization, high-red-tape government systems. That switching cost is rooted in org inertia + political accountability, NOT technology — so it survives the one thing that dissolves ordinary integration moats: models getting good enough to integrate themselves.

Key tension to track: the same frontier capability that pries open these systems is also what can detonate Anthropic's longest-duration asset — trust/compliance access (see Mythos/Fable suspension). Capability opens the window; safety positioning is what they bank during it.

Not investable directly (still private). But it reprices the whole 2B2G AI stack — and tells you which layer to underwrite when it is. Watch FDE-type hiring and contract language shifting from "subscription" to "custom deployment."

It was inevitable.

After GPT-5.6 Sol and Mythos, frontier models are no longer just software products.

They are becoming national assets; protected, governed, and restricted.

Korea has been talking about sovereign AI for over a year. The initiatives are real. But whether they can keep up with SOTA models remains an open question.

As we approach the singularity, a new productivity wall is being built between nations.

AI is starting to look less like software, and more like manufacturing.

From open source and sharing, to tariffs, export controls, and anti-leakage walls.

The frontier is now geopolitical.

Good new first: Sol is a smart, efficient, and a significant step forward. It is the same price as GPT-5.5. Also launching in the GPT-5.6 family is Terra, with 5.5-level performance at half the price.

Bad news: at the request of the US government, it is launching today in limited preview instead of the open access launch we were planning on. We are working with the government to get to general availability as fast as we can.

I think it is quite reasonable to roll out models--especially as they reach significant new levels of capability--in this way. It fits with our long-held strategy of iterative deployment. But this isn't quite the process that we think is optimal.

Now we will with the government to attempt to get to a transparent, reliable process for early access, and to ensure that as long as our safeguards work as intended we can release widely. We want to be a reliable, dependable partner that works with all stakeholders, and we also want to live by our mission of benefiting all of humanity. I believe the government shares most of our goals, and that they are overall doing a good job in a very difficult situation.

We will work as quickly as we can to get this model in your hands and we hope you will love it.

data.text:
🇨🇳🧠🤔US thought it owned AI cyber high ground - China had other plans
  
China’s AI is closing the gap on the US in cutting edge cybersecurity. Zhipu AI’s new GLM‑5.2 model matches the performance of Anthropic's Mythos in some aspects of bug detection, reports WSJ.
 
🔶GLM-5.2 is an open-weight model that can be downloaded, run, and customized by anyone on their own hardware

🔶It’s ranked as one of the 10 most-used AI models, according to OpenRouter data

🔶In select tests, GLM‑5.2 beat Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8, which came out just weeks ago, according to cybersecurity firm Semgrep.
 
With refined prompts, GLM-5.2 stands shoulder-to-shoulder with Mythos, a closed-door demo which recently left Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-NY) "scared."
 
The AI autonomously found and exploited a bank vulnerability when instructed by Anthropic to empty accounts — and then figured out how to patch it.

🇺🇸 Mythos also churned out a detailed kidnapping plan in 30 seconds and warned that agentic AI could be used to target critical infrastructure, such as shutting down gas pipelines — all with minimal human input.
 
🔍 Earlier this month, China’s 360 Security Technology also unveiled its new cyber tool – Tulongfeng – touted proudly as “China’s Mythos. Tulongfeng has reportedly already identified 3,432 software vulnerabilities.
 
🇨🇳 Chinese frontier models have moved from around 60% of the intelligence level of leading US models in 2023 toward roughly 90% today, according to Artificial Analysis data.

As the capability gap shrinks, the implications are profound, since the bull case for sky-high US AI valuations — built on an unassailable capability moat — now faces real pressure.
 
➡️ Affordable, capable Chinese alternatives offer cost efficiency

➡️ Open-weight accessibility accelerates innovation across the broader AI community (outside elite labs)

➡️ Microsoft and others are exploring integrations on their platforms
 
“China is making sure that the gap becomes smaller and smaller over time,” Lior Div, CEO of US cybersecurity firm 7AI, noted.

This surge arrives amid US self-imposed hurdles — OpenAI throttling GPT-5.6 access over security jitters, Anthropic models like Fable 5 and Mythos 5 restricted for foreigners, and Pentagon autonomous kill-switch debates.
 
China's models aren't just increasingly competitive — they are liberating powerful tools from gated Western enclaves.
